extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and novelists learning worldbuilding craft
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and evaluating fictional settings and worldbuilding that feel vivid, coherent, and integral to character and plot. Covers sensory detail, internal consistency, cultural/economic/political layers, techniques for revealing information, and common failure modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensory richness
rubrics_metrics.description: engages all 5 senses, not just sight
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use smells, sounds, tastes, touch as anchors so scenes feel lived-in rather than purely visual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific over generic
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose concrete, particular details (e.g., 'the marketplace at Tasrekh') rather than generic labels to create vividness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mood/atmosphere coherent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the sensory and descriptive elements of place reinforce the scene's emotional tenor rather than contradict it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting affects character
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how environment influences characters' habits, beliefs, fears, and desires so setting helps define character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting affects plot
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use locale, infrastructure, resources, and local conflicts to create plot opportunities and obstacles rather than treating setting as backdrop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain consistent application of the world's physical, social, and magical rules; avoid invoking rules only when convenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied rather than explained
rubrics_metrics.description: no infodumps; details earn their place
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveal history and rules through consequences, objects, and character interactions rather than lengthy exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: different locations have different feels (Hogwarts vs. Gringotts)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design distinct locations with contrasting sensory palettes, social norms, and atmospheres to enrich the world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living, evolving world
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray institutions, markets, and social dynamics as active and changing rather than static backgrounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verisimilitude
rubrics_metrics.description: even fantasy worlds feel internally true
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when imaginary, the world should feel plausible according to its own rules and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify temporal anchors to situate action and inform lighting, weather, social rhythms, and historical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define scale of setting from broad geography to intimate interiors to orient readers and shape scene dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weather and climate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use weather and long-term climate patterns to affect mood, logistics, economy, and characters' daily lives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed social structures and norms in scenes to show how people live and interact in the world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cultural artifacts and practices to communicate values, history, and difference between groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show who controls resources, what work looks like, and how scarcity or abundance shapes behavior and power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate governance, factionalism, and political pressures as drivers of character choices and plot events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical layers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imply past events, ruins, legends, and institutional histories that leave traces shaping the present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iceberg principle
rubrics_metrics.description: know far more than you write
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have extensive unseen world detail; reveal only what is needed for the story, but let the unseen inform the visible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveal organically
rubrics_metrics.description: show consequences of history rather than recounting it
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let history and world rules emerge through plot, character behavior, and artifacts instead of exposition-heavy summaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific names and details
rubrics_metrics.description: "the marketplace at Tasrekh" is more vivid than "the marketplace"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use memorable proper names and distinctive specifics to ground locations and make them feel real.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensory anchors
rubrics_metrics.description: smell of fish, sound of bells, taste of yam porridge
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach consistent sensory cues to locations or cultures so readers can inhabit the space more fully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telling objects
rubrics_metrics.description: a single household item can imply a culture
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use objects as shorthand for broader social, economic, or historical truths about the world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character-mediated POV
rubrics_metrics.description: what the character notices reveals their world
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter descriptive detail through a character's priorities and perspective to reveal both setting and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travelogue scenes (failure mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Travelogue scenes that pause story for description
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid scenes that stop narrative momentum to display setting; integrate description into action and stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic "medieval European" fantasy (failure mode)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of defaulting to un-differentiated medieval Europe; create distinctive cultural and environmental details.

rubrics_metrics.name: World rules invoked only when convenient (failure mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: World rules invoked only when convenient
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't introduce rules or mechanics only as plot conveniences; adhere to established logic throughout the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Map-without-people fantasy (failure mode)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid creating detailed geography that lacks social life; populate maps with cultures, economies, and routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future tech that doesn't change the human stakes (failure mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Future tech that doesn't change the human stakes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you add technology or fantastical innovations, show how they alter daily life, power, and relationships rather than dressing characters in gadgets only cosmetically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign settings used as "exotic backdrop" (failure mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign settings as "exotic backdrop" without lived texture
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using other cultures merely for color; render them with lived texture, nuance, and particular social realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting as character
rubrics_metrics.description: the place has agency, mood, history
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat setting like a cast member with agency and influence; examples include Yoknapatawpha (Faulkner), Macondo (García Márquez), Brixton (Smith), Kerala (Roy).
